sections.history: Thoovainathar stands on the East Street of Tiruvarur, within the great temple town that is the heart of the Kaveri delta's Shaiva tradition. Its historical name is Arur Paravaiyunmandali — 'Arur, the mansion-quarter of Paravai' — recalling Paravai Nachiyar, the wife of the saint Sundarar, who lived in Tiruvarur. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, counted among the shrines of the southern Kaveri. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of the town, the shrine enshrines Thoovainathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Panchin Mennadiyal — in Sanskrit Mridupada Nayaki, 'she whose feet are soft as cotton' — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. Though modest beside the vast Thyagaraja temple nearby, it keeps its own place in the sacred map of Tiruvarur.
sections.legends: The historical name joins the shrine to the story of Sundarar and Paravai Nachiyar, his first wife, whose home was in Tiruvarur — a story in which, by the tradition of the town, Shiva himself walked as a messenger between the saint and his beloved. The goddess's tender name, Panchin Mennadiyal, 'she of the cotton-soft feet,' belongs to the gentle grace of Devi. As one shrine within the great Tiruvarur, its own sthala purana is woven into the larger lore of the town.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims to the great temples of Tiruvarur, following the Paadal Petra trail, include Thoovainathar among the shrines of the town.
sections.experience: At Thoovainathar the pilgrim finds a quieter shrine within the great Tiruvarur, rich in the memory of Sundarar and Paravai. Before Thoovainathar and the cotton-soft-footed Panchin Mennadiyal, the visitor touches a corner of the town's vast Shaiva story, where even the smaller temples carry a famous name.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thoovainathar is on the East Street of Tiruvarur town, within easy reach of the great Thyagaraja temple. Tiruvarur has its own railway station and bus stand; the shrine is a short walk or auto ride within the town.
